cards.name: Per-weapon maximum run speed
cards.summary: Every weapon sets the top ground speed of its holder. Rifles are slower than knives and pistols, and scoping a sniper rifle slows the player further.
cards.behavior: The player speed cap is recomputed whenever the weapon, zoom or round state changes. The order of checks is fixed. A spectator gets a very high cap. During the freeze period the cap is 1 unit per second, so nobody can walk. A VIP gets a fixed cap. Otherwise the active weapon reports its own cap, and a player with no weapon gets a default. The movement step then scales the requested move command down so that its length never exceeds the cap. The cap is a hard limit on wish speed only. It does not clamp speed gained from jumps, knockback or falls. Heavier weapons give lower caps, for example the machine gun and the main assault rifle of the terrorist side. Sniper rifles use a lower cap while zoomed. A tactical shield lowers the knife and grenade caps. Use one data table of weapon to cap and call one function after every equip or zoom change.

cards.name: Ground friction and acceleration
cards.summary: Walking uses speed-proportional friction with a stop-speed floor and a capped acceleration. The server locks the three tuning values at every round restart.
cards.behavior: Each ground move step first applies friction. The speed drop equals the friction coefficient times the larger of the current speed and the stop-speed floor, times the frame time. Friction is skipped below 0.1 units per second. A short probe is cast 16 units ahead of the feet along the velocity and 34 units down. When the probe finds no floor, the friction coefficient is multiplied by an engine edge-friction factor, so players brake near ledges. The engine supplies that factor, and this repository does not set it. Acceleration then adds speed along the wished direction. The amount added is the shortfall between the wished speed and the speed already moving that way, limited to acceleration times frame time times wished speed. The result is a quick start with no overshoot past the cap. The game rules code writes the three values at every round restart: acceleration 5, friction 4 and stop speed 75. These are the effective values in retail play. Treat them as constants in a clone. The wished speed is first clamped to the weapon speed cap. Ground speed below 1 unit per second is zeroed.

cards.name: Air acceleration cap for strafing
cards.summary: In the air the wished speed is clamped to 30 units per second for the add-speed test. Players can curve a jump but cannot gain large speed along one direction.
cards.behavior: Air movement skips friction. It reuses the ground acceleration idea with one change. The wished speed used to find the shortfall is clamped to 30 units per second. The amount actually added each step still scales with the full wished speed, the air acceleration value and the frame time. A player who turns the view while holding a sideways key therefore adds small steady speed along a changing direction. This is the strafe-turn used in jump routes. The air acceleration value comes from the engine move variables, not from this repository. The step is dead when the player is dead or in a water jump.

constants.name: air wished-speed cap
constants.unit: units per second used in the add-speed test

cards.name: Jump launch speed and landing stamina penalty
cards.summary: A jump sets the vertical speed so the apex is 45 units high. Landing and walking within about 1.3 seconds of a jump slows horizontal speed, and jumping again in that window gives a lower hop.
cards.behavior: The jump launch speed is the square root of two times gravity times the wanted height. Gravity is 800 units per second squared and the wanted height is 45 units, which gives about 268 units per second upward. The height comes from a server variable with default 45, and a crouching long-jump module uses 56. A jump needs the jump key to be released first, so holding the key does not pogo, unless the auto bunny-hop variable is on (default off). A player cannot jump while the duck transition is running. After a jump the stamina timer starts at 1315.789 milliseconds and counts down per command. While the timer is above zero, each ground move step multiplies the horizontal velocity by a ratio that starts at 0.75 and rises linearly to 1. The ratio is 1 minus the timer times 0.00019. Because the multiply runs once per ground step, its strength depends on the command rate. A restore-rate variable (default 0, off) can normalize it. A second jump inside the window also scales the new vertical launch speed by the same ratio. In water at waist depth or more the jump key swims upward instead: 100 units per second in water, 80 in slime and 50 in lava. Clones should keep the stamina timer as a separate field and tick it in milliseconds.

constants.name: gravity used in the launch formula
stamina timer after a jump
constants.unit: milliseconds, counted down per movement command

constants.name: stamina penalty slope
constants.unit: percent per second of remaining timer

cards.name: Anti bunny-hop speed crop at jump start
cards.summary: When a jump starts above 1.2 times the weapon speed cap, the whole velocity is scaled down to 0.8 times that limit. The effect is off when the bunny-hop variable is set.
cards.behavior: At the moment a jump starts the code measures the full velocity length. The limit is 1.2 times the current weapon speed cap. If the speed is at or below the limit, nothing happens. If it is above, the velocity is multiplied by 0.8 times the limit divided by the speed. The result is a speed of 0.96 times the weapon cap, so a chain of hops cannot build speed. The check runs once per jump and not while airborne. A server variable named sv_enablebunnyhopping, default 0, skips the crop. Use the same shape in a clone: limit equals factor times cap, and the new speed equals a fixed fraction of the limit.

constants.name: limit factor
constants.unit: multiple of the weapon speed cap

constants.name: crop fraction
constants.unit: multiple of the limit that the speed is cut to

cards.name: Crouch transition, hull height and crouch speed
cards.summary: Crouching shrinks the collision box from 72 to 50 units tall, lowers the eye from 17 to 12 units, and cuts move commands to one third. The slide takes 0.4 seconds.
cards.behavior: While the duck key is held the forward and side move commands are scaled by 0.333, so crouch walking runs at about a third of the weapon cap. When the key is first pressed on the ground a duck timer starts at 1000 milliseconds and the player enters the transition. The eye height is eased along a spline from the standing value to the crouched value. The transition ends when 0.4 seconds have passed, or at once if the player is in the air. At the end the hull switches to the small box and the origin drops 18 units on the ground so the feet stay put. The jump key is ignored while the transition runs. Releasing the key tries to stand: the code tests the tall box at the raised spot and stays crouched until the space is free. The standing hull is 32 units wide on each axis and 72 tall, from 36 below to 36 above the origin. The crouched hull is also 32 wide and runs from 18 below to 32 above the origin. Eye height above the origin is 17 standing and 12 crouched. Crouched steps are quieter and slower.

cards.name: Fall damage from landing speed
cards.summary: Landing faster than 500 units per second hurts. Damage grows linearly and reaches the kill level for a full-health player at about 980 units per second.
cards.behavior: While airborne the movement step stores the downward speed each command. On the first server frame after landing, the player code checks that speed. Below 250 units per second there is no effect. Between 250 and about 290 the landing stays silent. Above about 290 the view gets a punch and a landing sound plays. Above 500 the rules object returns damage equal to the excess speed times 100 over 600, times 1.25. A fall at 1100 units per second would deal 125. A player with 100 health dies from a fall at about 980. The damage is applied as fall damage, which ignores armor. Landing in water gives no damage. A server variable mp_falldamage (default 1) can switch the whole effect off. The pitch punch is reset to zero after damage. Sound steps use a separate 580 value that does not change the damage.

constants.unit: units per second of downward speed

cards.name: Ladder climbing
cards.summary: On a ladder volume gravity stops, the move keys drive a climb along the ladder face at up to 200 units per second, and jumping pushes the player away at 270.
cards.behavior: A brush model with the ladder content type switches the player to flying movement while the player hull overlaps it. Gravity is zeroed. The move keys build a velocity from the view direction. That velocity is split into a part into the face and a part along it. The part into the face turns into vertical motion, so looking up and pressing forward climbs and looking down descends. With no key the velocity is zero, so the player holds on the ladder. The climb speed is the smaller of 200 and the weapon cap, and it is scaled by the crouch multiplier when crouched. Pressing jump ends the ladder state and sets the velocity to 270 units per second along the ladder surface normal. Standing on the floor and pressing away from the ladder adds a 200 unit push. The step sound on a ladder is quieter and slower.

constants.name: jump-off speed
constants.unit: units per second along the ladder normal

cards.name: Footstep noise by speed and posture
cards.summary: Players are silent at or below 150 units per second. Faster steps play every 300 milliseconds, crouched steps are 100 milliseconds slower and 35 percent as loud.
cards.behavior: The step sound code runs after the move step. If the speed is 150 units per second or lower, it sets a 400 millisecond wait and plays nothing. This is how walking with the quiet key stays silent. Above 150, a step plays when the timer reaches zero. The timer is 300 milliseconds on most surfaces, 350 on a ladder, 600 when wading and 300 when sloshing. Ducking or ladders add 100 milliseconds. A crouched player past the first part of the duck timer also plays at 35 percent volume. Volume is 0.5 on concrete and metal and 0.7 on vents. The result is a clear trade-off: moving fast is loud and moving slow is silent. The bot hearing card shows how enemy AI uses these steps.

constants.name: extra interval when crouched or on a ladder

cards.name: Hit slowdown and knockback flinch
cards.summary: Taking a hit from a player cuts ground speed to half or 65 percent, then recovers by 0.01 per server frame. Some heavy weapons also push a standing victim away.
cards.behavior: A velocity modifier starts at 1. When a player damages another player, the victim modifier is set to 0.5. If the victim is standing and was not hit on a leg, and the attacker holds a heavy weapon from a fixed list, the modifier is 0.65 instead and the victim is pushed away from the attacker. The push is 170 units per second, only when the victim speed is below 300. While the victim is on the ground, the pre-think step adds 0.01 to the modifier and multiplies the whole velocity by it, every server frame, until it returns to 1. Because the multiply repeats each frame, the first frames cut speed very hard. The recovery is frame based, so it depends on the server frame rate, which this repository does not set. Crouching victims never get the large flinch. The knockback value is a server variable with default 170.

cards.name: Rifle spread from movement, air and shots fired
cards.summary: Automatic weapons pick a spread from three states: in the air, running, or still. Running and air spread scale with an accuracy value that grows with the cube of consecutive shots.
cards.behavior: Each rifle trigger pull picks one of three spread formulas. In the air the spread is a base value plus 0.4 times the accuracy value. On the ground above 140 units per second the spread is the base plus 0.07 times accuracy. Standing or walking slowly the spread is only a small coefficient times accuracy, so accuracy still matters. The assault rifle uses base 0.04 and coefficients 0.4, 0.07 and 0.0275. The accuracy value is the cube of the consecutive shot count divided by a per-weapon divisor, plus 0.35, capped at 1.25. The divisor is 200 for the assault rifle, 220 for the carbine, 215 for the bullpup and 175 for the machine gun and the 5.7 submachine gun. It resets to 0.2 on deploy and on reload. A burst is a short spray, and the cube makes the first few shots tight and later shots wild. After the player releases the trigger, the shot counter stays for 0.4 seconds and then drops by one every 0.0225 seconds, so tapping resets accuracy slowly. The counter is capped at 15 on release. The cube divide is float math in the default build and integer math in the parity build, so the small-count shots keep the 0.35 floor longer in the parity build. The final spread is a unitless tangent. The bullet direction is the aim plus x times spread along the right vector plus y times spread along the up vector. Each of x and y is the sum of two uniform samples in minus 0.5 to plus 0.5, so aim error clusters near the center. The player random seed from the user command drives the samples, so a predicting client and the server agree.

constants.unit: unitless tangent added to the air spread

constants.unit: units per second of ground speed

constants.unit: unitless added after the cube term

cards.name: Pistol accuracy that recovers with time between shots
cards.summary: Pistols are semi-automatic. Spread is a state coefficient times one minus an accuracy value, and the accuracy value falls when shots come faster than a set interval.
cards.behavior: A pistol fires once per trigger press. The shot counter blocks a held trigger until it is released, and for pistols the counter resets to zero on release. The accuracy value starts at 0.9 for the large pistol and 0.92 for the service pistol. After each shot the code subtracts (interval minus time since the last shot) times a factor, so rapid taps lose accuracy and slow taps regain it. The value is clamped to a band: 0.55 to 0.9 for the large pistol and 0.6 to 0.92 for the service pistol. The spread is a state coefficient times (1 minus accuracy). The state coefficients for the large pistol are 1.5 in the air, 0.25 when moving at all, 0.115 crouched and 0.13 standing. A crouched, still, slow-tapping player is the most precise. The cycle time passed in is reduced by 0.075 seconds inside the fire function, so the true minimum interval is 0.225 seconds for the large pistol and 0.15 seconds for the service pistol. The service pistol has a silencer state with different coefficients: silenced 1.3, 0.25, 0.125 and 0.15, unsilenced 1.2, 0.225, 0.08 and 0.1.

constants.name: large pistol accuracy loss interval
constants.unit: seconds of reference interval between shots

constants.name: large pistol accuracy loss factor
constants.unit: accuracy per second of interval deficit

cards.name: Sniper scope zoom, unscoped penalty and move-shot spread
cards.summary: Scoped sniper shots are nearly perfect only when still. Moving or jumping adds large spread, an unscoped shot adds a flat penalty, and zooming slows the player.
cards.behavior: The secondary button steps the field of view through zoom levels. The heavy sniper rifle goes 90, 40, 10 and back. The light sniper rifle and the two auto snipers go 90, 40, 15 and back. Each toggle waits 0.3 seconds. The movement speed cap drops while any zoom is active. When the player fires while zoomed, the zoom is removed for the shot and restored when the next attack delay ends. If the player was not zoomed, a flat extra spread is added: 0.08 for the heavy rifle and 0.025 for the light rifle and the auto sniper. The base spread depends on state. The heavy rifle uses 0.85 in the air, 0.25 above 140 units per second, 0.1 above 10, 0.0 crouched and 0.001 standing. The light rifle uses 0.2 in the air, 0.075 above 170, 0.0 crouched and 0.007 standing. The heavy rifle cycle time is 1.45 seconds and the light rifle 1.25. Each shot kicks the view up by 2 degrees. The auto sniper rifle has a different model: its spread is multiplied by one minus an accuracy value that grows with the time since the last shot at 0.3 per second from 0.55 up to 0.98.

cards.name: Recoil view kick with growing vertical and alternating lateral drift
cards.summary: Every shot adds a vertical view kick that grows with the shot count up to a cap, plus a lateral kick that flips direction at random. Bullets fly along the kicked view.
cards.behavior: The kick function takes seven numbers: a base vertical kick, a base lateral kick, a vertical growth per shot, a lateral growth per shot, a vertical cap, a lateral cap and a direction-change odds value. The first shot uses only the bases. Later shots add the growth times the shot count. The vertical kick is subtracted from the view pitch and cannot push the pitch beyond the cap. The lateral kick moves the view yaw in the current direction, limited by the lateral cap. After each shot the direction flips with odds of 1 in (change value plus 1). The code applies the kick before the next shot, and the bullet direction is built from the view angle plus this punch angle, so recoil moves where the next bullet goes. The punch angle then decays: its length falls by 10 plus half its current length, per second, scaled by the command time. The assault rifle has four parameter sets. Standing: 1.0, 0.375, 0.175, 0.0375, 5.75, 1.75, 8. Moving: 1.5, 0.45, 0.225, 0.05, 6.5, 2.5, 7. In the air: 2.0, 1.0, 0.5, 0.35, 9.0, 6.0, 5. Crouched: 0.9, 0.35, 0.15, 0.025, 5.5, 1.5, 9. Crouching lowers the caps. Jumping raises everything. The carbine uses gentler sets, and snipers use one fixed 2 degree vertical kick. The retail build clamps the kicks with a different order of tests than the extended build.

cards.name: Wall and body penetration by bullet type and surface
cards.summary: A bullet may pass through surfaces. The caliber sets how deep it skips into a wall and how far it can still penetrate. The surface sets how much power and damage it keeps.
cards.behavior: The bullet trace loop runs while the penetration count is not zero. Each weapon passes its own count: 1 for light weapons, 2 for rifles and the large pistol, 3 for snipers. Each hit uses one count, including a hit on a player. The caliber table gives a penetration power in units and a penetration range in units. After a hit the next trace starts at the impact point plus the aim direction times the power, so the power is how many units of wall the bullet skips. If the hit distance is beyond the penetration range, penetration stops. The surface type multiplies the power: metal 0.15, concrete 0.25, grate and vent 0.5, tile 0.65, computer 0.4. Wood keeps the full power. The surface also sets a damage keep factor for the next segment: 0.2 for metal, 0.4 for grate, 0.45 for vent and computer, 0.3 for tile, 0.6 for wood, and 0.5 by default. If the hit entity is not a world brush, or this was the last allowed hit, the power becomes 42, the damage keep factor 0.75 and the remaining distance is cut to 0.75. Otherwise the remaining distance is cut to 0.5 on a world brush. A shield hit stops the bullet. The damage value is an integer, so it truncates at every step. Wall hits also draw decals. A server hook can mark entities as not penetrable.

constants.name: last hit or body damage keep factor

cards.name: Per-weapon base damage and distance falloff
cards.summary: Damage is a base number times a per-weapon range factor raised to the hit distance divided by 500 units. The result is an integer.
cards.behavior: At each bullet impact the code multiplies the current damage by the weapon range modifier raised to the power of (hit distance divided by 500). A modifier near 1 loses little over distance, and a low modifier collapses damage fast. Pistols have low modifiers, rifles and snipers high ones. The hit distance is measured on the current trace segment, not as a running total, because the remaining distance is shortened and re-measured after each penetration. The product is stored in an integer, so every step drops the fraction. The base damage values are the numbers in the table below. The maximum bullet reach is 8192 units for rifles and 4096 for pistols with the large calibers. A shotgun uses a separate linear falloff, see the shotgun card.

cards.name: Hit-group damage multipliers and hit view kick
cards.summary: Where the bullet lands changes the damage: head 4 times, stomach 1.25 times, chest and arms 1 times, legs 0.75 times. Unarmored hits also kick the victim view.
cards.behavior: The hit group comes from the trace result and is stored on the victim for later use by armor and flinch. The multipliers are applied before armor. A head hit multiplies damage by 4. A stomach hit multiplies it by 1.25. Chest and arm hits do not change it. Leg hits multiply by 0.75. Explosions, fall damage and similar types force the generic group, so they ignore these multipliers. A shield hit zeroes the damage and plays a ricochet. If the victim has no matching armor, bullets also kick the victim view: a head hit kicks the pitch by minus 0.5 times the damage, capped at minus 12 degrees, plus a random roll of up to 9 degrees either way. A chest or stomach hit kicks the pitch by minus 0.1 times the damage, capped at minus 4. Armor changes the blood and spark effects. A helmet on a head hit makes sparks instead of blood. Teammate hits still run this code, but later steps decide if damage applies.

constants.name: head hit roll cap
constants.unit: degrees, lower limit of a symmetric clamp

cards.name: Armor absorption with per-weapon penetration ratio
cards.summary: Armor sends a share of the damage to the armor pool. The share is set by the attacker weapon, so high-penetration weapons ignore more armor. Helmets cover the head.
cards.behavior: The base ratio is 0.5, the share of damage that reaches health, and the armor bonus is 0.5. The ratio is multiplied by an attacker weapon value: 1.55 for the main assault rifle and the light assault rifle, 1.4 for the carbine and the bullpup rifles, 1.95 for the heavy sniper, 1.65 and 1.45 for the auto snipers, 1.7 for the light sniper and the knife, 1.5 for the machine gun, the large pistol and the 5.7 guns, 1.25 for the 228 pistol, 1.05 for the auto pistol and the dual pistols, and 0.95 for the 10 mm submachine gun. A shield on the victim adds 0.2 to the base ratio, and a VIP halves the base ratio. Health damage equals ratio times damage. The armor lost equals (damage minus health damage) times the bonus. If the armor pool is smaller than needed, the pool goes to zero and the rest passes to health at two health points per armor point. Head hits use armor only when a helmet is present. Legs are never covered. Fall and drown damage ignore armor. Explosions use a different branch: the ratio stays 0.5, so half the damage reaches health, the armor loses a quarter of the damage, and an empty pool passes the remainder to health. The step that doubles the armor bonus for blast damage sits after that branch returns, so it never runs for explosions. Full armor holds 100 points, and a VIP spawns with 200.

constants.unit: share of damage that reaches health

constants.name: armor bonus
constants.unit: armor points lost per damage point absorbed

cards.name: Shotgun pellet volley with linear falloff
cards.summary: The pump shotgun fires 9 pellets and the auto shotgun 6. Each pellet does 20 damage, scaled down linearly over its reach, with a wide fixed cone.
cards.behavior: A shotgun shot makes one trace per pellet. Each pellet gets its own random offset with the same triangular spread as rifle shots, but with a fixed cone per axis: 0.0675 for the pump gun and 0.0725 for the auto gun. The cone does not depend on movement. The reach is 3000 units for the pump gun and 3048 for the auto gun. A pellet damage is the base 20 times (1 minus the hit fraction of the reach), so a point-blank pellet does about 20 and a pellet at the end of the reach does close to 0. All pellet hits are summed into one damage call for each target. Pellets do not penetrate. The pump gun cycle is 0.875 seconds and the auto gun 0.25. The view kicks up 4 to 6 degrees on the ground and 8 to 11 in the air for the pump gun, and 3 to 5 or 7 to 10 for the auto gun. The shotgun reloads one shell at a time and can be interrupted by firing.

constants.name: pump gun pellet damage
constants.unit: health points per pellet before falloff

cards.name: Three-round burst mode for the auto pistol and the French rifle
cards.summary: The secondary button toggles a three-round burst. The remaining shots follow on a fixed timer, with a long gap before the next burst.
cards.behavior: In burst mode the first shot fires on the normal path and queues two more. The queued shots fire from the weapon update loop at fixed intervals. For the auto pistol the first follow-up comes 0.1 seconds after the first shot and the next one 0.1 seconds later, with a fixed spread of 0.05 and the pistol damage and range factor. For the rifle the first follow-up comes 0.05 seconds after the first shot, the next ones every 0.1 seconds, and all three use the spread of the first shot. Burst shots on the rifle do 34 damage against 30 in automatic mode. After the burst the weapon waits 0.5 seconds (pistol) or 0.55 seconds (rifle) before the next trigger pull is accepted. Single-fire pistol mode has a 0.2 second cycle minus 0.05. The rifle in automatic mode adds a 0.01 spread penalty. The burst mode is stored in a weapon state bit that survives holstering. Reloading is blocked while queued shots remain.
capabilities: queued follow-up shots on a timer

cards.name: Knife slash, stab and backstab
cards.summary: The primary button swings for 15 damage and the secondary stabs for 65. A stab to the back of a target does three times that. A swing after an idle gap does 20.
cards.behavior: A swing traces a line 48 units ahead, and falls back to a small hull sweep when the line misses. A stab traces 32 units. A swing does 15 damage, or 20 when the previous attack ended more than 0.4 seconds ago. A stab does 65. A stab that hits a player multiplies the damage by 3 when the two players face the same way in the flat plane. The test is a dot product above 0.8 between the attacker forward and the victim forward, which is a cone of about 37 degrees. The next attack delay is 0.35 seconds after a swing miss, 0.4 after a swing hit, 1.0 after a stab miss and 1.1 after a stab hit. Hits go through the same hit-group code as bullets, with the bullet damage type, so armor applies. The knife has the top speed cap of 250. A shield user has a slower cap and a different knife animation.

constants.name: backstab facing dot threshold
constants.unit: cosine of the angle between forwards

cards.name: Friendly fire scaling and team-kill penalty
cards.summary: Friendly fire is off by default. When on, team bullets do 35 percent damage in the extended build and team grenades 25 percent. A team kill costs the killer 3300 money.
cards.behavior: The friendly fire variable defaults to 0, so teammates do no damage to each other. With it on, the damage code looks at the attacker team. In the extended build, bullets are scaled by 0.35, other damage by 0.25 and grenades by 0.25, but a grenade that hurts its own thrower is not scaled. In the retail build every team hit is scaled by 0.35. Killing a teammate removes frags, takes 3300 money from the killer and counts a team kill. When the count reaches 3 (the default limit variable), the killer is kicked if the auto-kick variable is on. A hit on a teammate also tells all teammates who did it, at most once every 0.6 seconds. Damage on a teammate can also be refused if the damage rule says teammates cannot hurt each other.

constants.name: team bullet scale in the extended build

cards.name: High-explosive grenade throw, fuse and blast falloff
cards.summary: A thrown grenade explodes 1.5 seconds after release. Damage is 100 at the center and falls linearly to zero at 350 units. Armor and hit-group rules for blast use a separate branch.
cards.behavior: The throw speed is (90 minus the throw pitch after a small offset) times 6, capped at 750 units per second, and the thrower velocity is added. The grenade bounces with gravity scale 0.55 and friction 0.7, and a think function ticks every 0.1 seconds. In the last second it posts a danger sound for bots. At the fuse time the grenade runs the blast. Because the damage value is above 80, the radius is the damage times 3.5, so 350 units. Each entity inside the sphere takes the damage minus (distance times damage divided by radius), so the fall-off is linear from 100 to 0. The distance is measured from the grenade origin raised 1 unit to the entity origin, not to the nearest body part. The default build does not check line of sight for this damage, so walls do not shield a player in range, because the optional wall check cvar defaults to 0. A grenade in water only hurts entities in water, and out of water it skips swimmers. The blast uses the explosion damage type. For a player victim that type skips hit-group multipliers and uses the blast armor branch: half the damage reaches health and the armor loses a quarter of the damage. The blast also pushes the victim along the line from the grenade, scaled by 0.25 and a (2300 minus distance) term in the player code. Team grenade damage is zero when friendly fire is off, and 25 percent when on.

cards.name: Flashbang blind duration by distance and view direction
cards.summary: A flashbang blinds every player who has a clear line to the burst within 1500 units. Blind time scales down with distance and is longer when the victim faces the flash. Smoke is a separate cloud effect.
cards.behavior: The flashbang explodes 1.5 seconds after release and calls the flash routine with a strength of 4. The routine scans all players in a 1500 unit sphere. A victim must be alive and must not be in the water mismatch case. Two line traces must be clear: from the burst to the victim eyes (default build), and back. The adjusted strength is 4 minus distance times 4 divided by 1500, never below 0. If the victim faces the burst (the dot of the view forward and the direction to the burst is not negative), the screen fade alpha is 255, the fade time is strength times 3 seconds and the full-white hold is strength divided by 1.5 seconds. If the victim looks away, alpha is 200, the fade time is strength times 1.75 and the hold is strength divided by 3.5. At point-blank facing that gives up to 12 seconds of fade and 2.7 seconds of full white. A second flash that lands while the player is still held stacks: the old hold time is added when the new alpha is 255, and the longer fade and the higher alpha win. Teammate flash is on by default, and the thrower is also affected. The server also sets a blind timer on the player, at one third of the fade time, for bot logic. Smoke grenades use the same 1.5 second fuse and then play a client-side smoke particle event. The server does not store any smoke volume, so blocking of sight by smoke is a client and bot concern, and server line traces ignore it.

cards.name: Bomb plant, countdown, defuse and blast radius
cards.summary: Planting takes 3 seconds. The countdown defaults to 45 seconds. Defusing takes 10 seconds, or 5 with a kit, and stops when the defuser lets go. The blast reaches 1750 units.
cards.behavior: The carrier must hold the attack button inside a bomb zone while standing. The arming timer is 3 seconds and shows a progress bar, and the plant fails if the player lets go or leaves the zone. The countdown reads the server variable at plant time and clamps it to the range 10 to 90 seconds, with a default of 45. The bomb blinks every 2 seconds and beeps faster as the end nears, in four stages of a quarter of the timer each. A counter-terrorist uses the bomb to start a defuse. The defuse needs 10 seconds without a kit and 5 with one. The defuser must keep pressing use: if no use input arrives within 0.5 seconds, or the defuser leaves the ground, the defuse aborts and the timer resets on the next start. In the default build a defuse that is still running when the timer ends is also stopped, and the blast does not trigger once the defuse completes. The blast gives the explosion routine the map bomb radius value of 500 as the damage. The radius rule multiplies by 3.5, so the blast reaches 1750 units, and the damage falls linearly from 500 at the center to 0 at the edge. Map entities can change the radius value, capped at 2048. When the bomb blows, its owner gets 3 frags (the default of the give-frags variable). A successful defuse also gives the defuser frags. A defused bomb pays the CT team 3250 and still pays the terrorist team 800 for the plant. A blown bomb pays the terrorist team 3250.

cards.name: Round timer, freeze period and restart delay
cards.summary: Each round has a 6 second freeze time, then a 5 minute timer. A decided round restarts after 5 seconds. A planted bomb stops the timer from ending the round.
cards.behavior: The game reads the round variables on each restart. The round time is minutes times 60, so 300 seconds. The freeze time is clamped to 0 through 60 seconds, default 6. Two variables, both 1 by default, allow crouch and jump during the freeze. Setting one to 0 blocks that action in the freeze. When the freeze ends the timer counts down. The round ends when one team has no live players, when the objective completes (bomb blown, bomb defused, all hostages rescued, VIP or prisoner escape), or when the timer runs out. When the timer runs out and a bomb is planted, the round continues until the bomb blows or is defused. The end call sets the win state and a restart time of now plus the restart delay, which is 5 seconds by default. After that, the restart code respawns all players and entities. A full reset happens when the game restarts from a draw or by command. A full reset clears wins and loss streaks and gives only the start money. Team scores and the consecutive loss counts feed the economy card.

constants.name: round time default
constants.unit: minutes, multiplied by 60 to give seconds

capabilities: win conditions by objective or elimination

cards.name: Money, kill and win rewards, loss streak bonus and buy window
cards.summary: Players start with 800 money and hold at most 16000. A kill pays 300. The losing team gets a bonus that grows from 1500 by 500 per loss up to 3000. Buying is allowed for 90 seconds in a buy zone.
cards.behavior: Each reward is a constant in a rules array that the game reads at start. A kill of an enemy gives the killer 300. A round win gives the team 3000 on a plain elimination, 3250 for a blown or defused bomb, and 2500 for all hostages rescued. Each rescued hostage adds 750 to the CT team at round restart. The losing team receives a loser bonus. The first loss gives 1400, and the streak counter raises it by 500 after each further loss in a row, to a cap of 3000. When a team breaks a streak of two or more losses, the bonus resets to 1500 before the next increase. The rewards go to a team account and are paid to each player at restart. The buy window is the buy time in minutes times 60. The default is 1.5 minutes, 90 seconds, measured from the round start time, so it includes the freeze time. The default build allows a value below the retail minimum of 15 seconds. The buyer must be alive, in a buy zone, and not the VIP. Money is clamped between 0 and the cap on each change. Prices come from one table: the 7.62 mm rifle 2500, the carbine 3100, the heavy sniper 4750, the large pistol 650, the service pistol 500, a vest 650, a vest and helmet 1000, a defuse kit 200, the HE grenade 300, a flashbang 200 and a smoke grenade 300.

cards.name: Hostage follow, rescue and mistreatment penalties
cards.summary: A counter-terrorist presses use to make a hostage follow, and the hostage runs after them until it reaches a rescue zone. Hurting or killing a hostage costs money, and killing too many gets a terrorist kicked.
cards.behavior: The default build uses the older follow code, because the newer hostage AI variable defaults to 0. Only a counter-terrorist can use a hostage. A use toggles between follow and stand, with a 1 second cooldown. The first use of each hostage gives the user 150 money and the CT team account 100. The follow code aims at the leader feet position. The hostage stops when it is within 80 units of the leader. The move speed depends on the gap: under 110 units the speed equals the gap, from 110 up to 250 it is 300, and above 250 it is 400 units per second. A step that needs a jump sets an upward speed of 270. A hostage within the rescue radius of a rescue zone is rescued: it is removed, and the rescuer gets 1000 money. A hostage has 100 health and a 20 by 20 unit hull of height 62. Hit-group multipliers on a hostage differ from players: stomach and generic hits do 1.75 times damage and arm hits 0.75 times. Damage to a hostage costs the attacker 20 money per point. Killing one costs 20 times (25 plus the damage). A terrorist who kills 13 hostages is kicked in the default build. In the default build the CT team wins when all hostages are rescued, because the rescue ratio variable defaults to 1.0. The extra team rewards for hostages are on the economy card.

cards.name: Bot reaction delay, noticing chance and skill-based aim error
cards.summary: The computer players see an enemy only after a reaction delay from a 20-entry history sampled at 10 times per second. Their aim error shrinks as they hold still, up to a limit, and scales with a skill value.
cards.behavior: Bots are off unless a bot quota is set, because the quota variable defaults to 0. The full think runs every 0.1 seconds and commands run at 30 per second. Each full think pushes the best visible threat into a ring of 20 entries. The bot reads the entry that is "reaction time" old, with the profile reaction time rounded to whole steps and capped at 1.9 seconds. So a bot reacts to what it saw a fixed time ago. In the default build, a bot also rolls a chance to notice each visible enemy except its current target. A running enemy above 200 units per second is always noticed. A walking enemy is noticed with 100 to 75 percent (standing) or 90 to 60 percent (crouched), from 300 to 1000 units. A motionless crouched enemy gives 80 percent close and only 5 percent far. The chance is scaled by cover seen and by 0.5 plus half the skill, and has a floor of 0.1 percent. For aim, the bot sets an error cube per axis. The size is the range times the field of view ratio times 0.1, times one minus accuracy. Accuracy is the skill value, divided by one plus the turn fraction when it must turn to face the enemy (turn is the yaw change divided by 180). An unmoved view lets focus grow: the focus time is the larger of 2 or 5 times (1 minus accuracy) seconds, and focus can lift accuracy to at most 0.75. The error target is redrawn every 0.25 to 1.0 seconds and the actual offset moves 10 percent of the gap per update. A bot with a sniper rifle only zooms beyond 300 units and uses the high zoom beyond 1500, and fires only when still and zoomed.
